newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices steady despite weaker crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices steady despite weaker crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices held steady Monday despite a decline in crude and natural gas futures and sluggish demand from electric utilities.
"There are barrels out there but folks don't want to let them go," said one physical trader, referring to suppliers' reluctance that making more spot barrels available would keep prices depressed.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent gained another quarter to about $15.50-75 a barrel based on netback value of a Friday sale in Boston at $16.00, with April one percent paper holding at $15.75-16.00, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour grades notionally remained at $18.25-50 and $16.75, respectively. High sulphurs in New York also were unchanged.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent rose 25 cents higher to $14.25-50 in tandem with stronger values in New York and, while three percent notionally firmed to $13.38.
Forecasts of cold weather along the East Coast this week helped strengthened swing gas prices today.

At the New York City gate, day-ahead gas prices averaged five cents higher than Friday at $2.35 per million British thermal units or about 14.80 a barrel equivalent. Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed to the $2.00/mmBtu area or $12.60 a barrel.
NYMEX April crude futures settled down 37 cents at $20.92 per barrel.
Spot domestic resid business is expected to remain light with a number of participants attending the annual National Petroleum Refiners Association being held in San Antonio, Texas through Tuesday.
